footer_rights: Open source under AGPL-3.0. Built for teams that ship.
footer_blurb: Baton is deterministic workflow tracking for GitHub pull requests. It pins the state inside the thread and nudges the one person who can unblock the work.
hero_title_lead: Know whose turn it is on
hero_subtitle: Teams do not lose time writing code. They lose it waiting for reviews. Baton tracks the state of every open pull request, keeps a live status comment and a label in the thread, and sends one polite nudge when work stalls.
hero_proof_hint: A real Baton status comment cycles through states here.

simulator_hint: Choose a scenario to see the rule Baton applies.

stat_first_review_detail: Often 2 to 6 days across large repositories.
stat_first_review_source: Estimate drawn from public pull request data

stat_engine_detail: A pure state machine you can read, test, and reason about.
problem_subtitle: Responsibility on a pull request is implicit. Reviewers do not know they are blocking work. Authors do not know when a reviewer is waiting on a reply. The result is days of silent drift.
without_item_1_body: Reviewers get dozens of GitHub notifications a day and miss the first request.
without_item_2_body: The author fixes the comments, but GitHub never makes clear that the ball is back with the reviewer.
without_item_3_body: Engineers play detective in Slack, asking whether anyone can review pull request 182.
without_item_4_body: While the pull request waits, the base branch moves, tests rot, and rebases get painful.
with_item_1_title: One source of truth in the thread
with_item_1_body: A pinned card shows the state, the blocker, and the time in state at the top of the conversation.
with_item_2_body: When the author pushes commits after a review, Baton flips the state to re-review immediately.
with_item_3_body: Exactly one nudge, sent only after the grace period expires. No noise.
with_item_4_title: A queue for the next move
with_item_4_body: Reviewers see the pull requests waiting on them in one clean list. No searching required.
how_title: From a webhook to an unblocked pull request
how_subtitle: Baton is event driven. On every pull request event, and on a scheduled sweep as a safety net, it re-evaluates the state from standard GitHub APIs.
how_step_1_body: A GitHub webhook arrives with an HMAC-SHA256 signature. Baton reads review decisions, check conclusions, and mergeability. It does not read source diffs.
how_step_2_body: A pure state machine decides which of the eight canonical states applies, who owns the next move, and how long the pull request has waited in this state.
how_step_3_body: Baton updates its pinned comment and the baton state label, then, once the grace period passes, sends exactly one mention to the blocker.
how_note: Every webhook is verified with HMAC-SHA256 in constant time before any payload is parsed.
states_subtitle: See the exact rules Baton uses to assign ownership, labels, and thresholds from verifiable GitHub data.
states_silent_note: A silent state carries no GitHub label and no nudge. Baton stays quiet until the state changes.
features_subtitle: No noisy notifications and no dashboard nobody opens.
feature_status_card_body: Baton keeps one always current status comment at the top of the pull request. State, current owner, time in state, and the next unblocking action are always visible.
feature_labels_body: One baton label mirrors the pull request state in real time. It works with your existing GitHub search filters, notification routing, and triage workflows.
feature_nudges_body: At most one nudge per state, sent only after your grace period (for example 24 or 48 hours). It mentions only the person who can unblock the pull request, never the whole team.
feature_engine_body: Review decisions, review requests, checks, conflicts, and draft status feed a verifiable finite-state machine. No heuristics and no model guessing in the critical path.
feature_move_body: A clean developer dashboard groups pull requests by who must act next, so you can unblock teammates first thing in the morning.
feature_intelligence_body: Facts gathered from the GitHub API, each linked to the file or response it came from. A question the collected evidence cannot answer returns no evidence rather than a confident guess.
feature_permissions_body: Baton asks for Pull requests and Issues read and write for comments and labels, plus read only Checks, Metadata, and Contents. Contents is read to derive repository structure from the file tree, package manifest, and CODEOWNERS. Nothing is retained.
roi_title: How many hours is your team waiting?
roi_subtitle: Adjust the inputs to estimate the pull request waiting time Baton can remove for your team.
roi_notice: Estimates are directional, and Baton never reads your payroll data.
roi_formula_text: waiting hours removed per month = pull requests per month x hours saved per pull request, capped at 48 hours per pull request
roi_formula_note: Wait time is cap-limited, so the estimate stays conservative. It is a directional figure, not a promise.

security_title: Baton does not store your source code
security_body: Baton requests only the permissions it uses. Contents is read only and is used to read the file tree, the package manifest, and CODEOWNERS so Baton can describe how a repository is built. Those reads derive facts and are discarded, and no file contents are retained. Baton does not request Workflows or Secrets, and write access is limited to posting pull request comments and managing state labels.
security_matrix_caption: Baton GitHub App permissions, with access level, reason, and what is stored
security_row_1_why: Read review state, then update the single pinned comment and send nudges.
security_row_1_stored: Titles, numbers, author logins, and timestamps
security_row_2_why: Manage the baton state label on the pull request.
security_row_3_why: Read check conclusions so Baton never nudges reviewers on a failing build.
security_row_4_why: Read repository names, owner logins, and the default branch.
security_row_5_why: Read the file tree, package manifest, and CODEOWNERS to describe how a repository is built.
security_row_5_stored: Nothing. Reads are used to derive facts and then discarded.
security_row_6_why: Baton never requests Workflows or Secrets.

oauth_error_exchange_failed: GitHub rejected the sign-in credentials. Confirm the OAuth Client ID and Client secret, and that the callback URL is registered on the GitHub App.
oauth_error_github_api: GitHub could not complete the sign-in on its end (GitHub API error). Please try signing in again in a moment.
oauth_error_state_mismatch: Your sign-in request expired or was replayed. Please sign in again from the header. No harm done, just retry.
oauth_error_iss_mismatch: Sign-in was rejected for security reasons (unexpected OAuth issuer). Please try signing in again.
oauth_error_server_error: Sign-in could not be completed because the service database is currently unavailable. Please try again shortly.
oauth_error_db_misconfigured: Sign-in could not be completed because the service database is not configured on this deployment.
oauth_error_db_unreachable: Sign-in could not be completed because the service database could not be reached. Please try again shortly.
oauth_banner_unconfigured: GitHub sign-in is temporarily unavailable on this deployment because OAuth credentials are not configured. The GitHub App install flow still works.
oauth_banner_failed: GitHub sign-in failed. Please try again, or install the GitHub App directly from the header.
oauth_banner_denied: GitHub sign-in was cancelled. No problem, you can keep browsing or install Baton from the header.
select_prompt: Select a state to see its deterministic logic and nudge rule.
silent_state: No GitHub label, a silent state
matrix_awaiting_review_trigger: The pull request is open and not a draft, reviewers are requested or required by CODEOWNERS, and no review decision has been submitted yet.
matrix_awaiting_review_nudge: Sends at most one mention to the requested reviewers. The timer resets if the author pushes commits.
matrix_awaiting_review_action: Review the changes and submit approve or request changes.
matrix_awaiting_review_after_fix_trigger: A reviewer previously requested changes or commented, and the author has since pushed new commits.
matrix_awaiting_review_after_fix_nudge: Mentions only the reviewers whose feedback was addressed, sparing reviewers who already approved.
matrix_awaiting_review_after_fix_action: Verify the new commits resolve the earlier objections.
matrix_changes_required_trigger: At least one reviewer submitted request changes.
matrix_changes_required_nudge: Reviewers are not nudged. The author is reminded only after the grace period expires without new commits.
matrix_changes_required_action: Push changes or reply in the thread to resolve the concerns.
matrix_ci_failing_trigger: One or more required check suites or status contexts concluded as failure or timed out.
matrix_ci_failing_nudge: Reviewers are never nudged while checks are broken. The author is notified.
matrix_ci_failing_action: Inspect the logs, fix tests or lint, and push.
matrix_conflicts_trigger: GitHub reports the pull request as conflicting against the base branch.
matrix_conflicts_nudge: Alerts the author that the branch has drifted out of sync with the base.
matrix_conflicts_action: Rebase onto the base branch and resolve the conflicts.
matrix_ready_to_merge_trigger: Approved by the required reviewers, all checks passed, and no merge conflicts.
matrix_ready_to_merge_nudge: Nudges the author or maintainers if the pull request sits unmerged with every light green.
matrix_blocked_on_checks_trigger: Check suites are still in progress, so mergeability cannot be evaluated yet.
matrix_blocked_on_checks_nudge: A silent state. Nobody is nudged while automated jobs are still running.
matrix_blocked_on_checks_action: Wait for the checks to finish.
matrix_draft_trigger: The author marked the pull request as a draft.
matrix_draft_nudge: A silent state. Reviewers are never pinged on a work-in-progress draft.
matrix_draft_action: Mark it ready for review when it is prepared.
sim_nudge_dispatched: Nudge sent because the threshold passed
sim_1_next: Review the latest changes (3 commits, +142 and -18)
sim_1_trigger: Opened two days ago, reviewer requested, and no review submitted yet.
sim_1_cond_1: The pull request is open and not a draft.
sim_1_cond_2: A reviewer is requested and checks are green.
sim_1_cond_3: No review decision has been submitted yet.
sim_1_nudge: A friendly nudge: pull request 247 has been awaiting review for 48 hours. Could you take a look when you have a moment?
sim_1_rule: The first-response threshold has passed, so Baton sends exactly one nudge.
sim_2_next: Address review feedback on the auth middleware in src/auth/session.ts
sim_2_trigger: A reviewer requested changes, asking that token expiry handle UTC timezone skew.
sim_2_cond_1: The latest review decision is request changes.
sim_2_cond_2: The author has not pushed new commits since the review.
sim_2_nudge: The timer is active. The author is reminded once the grace period expires without new commits.
sim_2_rule: The baton passes to the author. Reviewers are not nudged.
sim_3_next: Verify the fix commit for UTC timezone skew
sim_3_trigger: The author pushed a new commit that enforces a UTC epoch in session verification.
sim_3_cond_2: The author pushed new commits after that review.
sim_3_nudge: The change is within the grace period, so no reminder is sent yet.
sim_3_rule: The state flips to re-review and the timer resets to zero.
sim_4_next: Fix the failing integration suite (exit code 1)
sim_4_trigger: A CI run failed on the integration test suite.
sim_4_cond_1: A required check suite concluded as failure.
sim_4_cond_2: Review is not the current blocker.
sim_4_nudge: Reviewers are spared. Baton avoids premature review requests while checks are red.
sim_4_rule: Regardless of review requests, the pull request is blocked on the author. Reviewers are never pinged for a broken build.
sim_5_trigger: A reviewer approved the change, all checks are green, and there are no conflicts.
sim_5_cond_1: A required reviewer approved the change.
sim_5_nudge: The pull request is green and unblocked. Once the ready-to-merge window elapses, Baton reminds the author or a maintainer.
sim_5_rule: No further review is needed. Someone just needs to perform the merge.
